Daily Brief

Russian missile strikes killed at least eight people in Kyiv overnight, damaging residential buildings, a children's hospital, and a school in what Ukrainian officials described as a 'massive attack' [BBC, Al Jazeera, France 24]. The strikes came as former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for wartime elections, presenting the biggest political challenge to President Zelensky since the 2022 invasion [BBC]. In economic news, Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan was sentenced to life in prison in China after pleading guilty to embezzlement and bribery, marking a decisive moment in the fallout from China's property crisis [BBC, Nikkei Asia, Financial Times]. President Trump escalated pressure on Iran, threatening 'tremendous economic consequences' on any country doing business with Tehran following the expiry of a 60-day ceasefire [BBC, Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, Australia expressed outrage after Israel declined to open criminal proceedings over the 2024 killing of aid worker Zomi Frankcom in the World Central Kitchen strike, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong summoning the Israeli ambassador [BBC, Al Jazeera]. In Central African Republic, over 100 people died when an illegal goldmine collapsed near the Cameroon border [The Guardian, Le Monde].

Evergrande Founder Hui Ka Yan Sentenced to Life in Prison as China Property Crisis Reaches Legal Conclusion

  • Hui Ka Yan, founder of collapsed property giant Evergrande, received life sentence and had all personal property confiscated after pleading guilty to embezzlement and corporate bribery
  • Shenzhen court fined Hui's former companies 15.82 billion yuan ($2.35 billion) for falsifying records and concealing debt
  • Other executives including Hui's two sons received sentences ranging from 22 months to 18 years
  • Once Asia's richest man, Hui rose from rural poverty to oversee Evergrande's aggressive expansion before its collapse shook China's property sector

Trump Threatens 'Economic D-Day' on Countries Doing Business with Iran

  • President Trump announced 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' targeting nations helping Iran, following expiry of 60-day ceasefire on Monday

Australia Summons Israeli Ambassador After IDF Declines Criminal Investigation into Aid Worker Deaths

  • Israel's military decided not to launch criminal investigation into April 2024 airstrike that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom and six World Central Kitchen colleagues

Over 100 Dead After Illegal Goldmine Collapses in Central African Republic
